q: Radioactivity is a spontaneous process of decay of heavy nuclei generating alpha particles, beta particles and _____ rays.
e: Radioactivity is a spontaneous process of decay of heavy nuclei generating alpha particles, beta particles and gamma rays. Radioactivity is when an unstable nucleus throws out alpha, beta, or gamma radiation to lose energy.

q: Alpha particles can be blocked by a few pieces of _____.
e: Alpha particles can be blocked by a few pieces of paper. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: Beta particles pass through paper but are stopped by _____ foil.
e: Beta particles pass through paper but are stopped by aluminium foil. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Gamma rays are the most difficult to stop and require concrete, _____, or other heavy shielding.
e: Gamma rays are the most difficult to stop and require concrete, lead, or other heavy shielding. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The majority of background radiation occurs naturally from minerals and a small fraction comes from _____ elements.
e: The majority of background radiation occurs naturally from minerals and a small fraction comes from inert elements. Background radiation is the ionising radiation that is already around you from rocks, air, and space.

q: Cosmic radiation from _____ also contributes to the background radiation around us.
e: Cosmic radiation from space also contributes to the background radiation around us. The core: core electrons stay inner and do not bond.

q: Traces of radioactive materials can be found in the human body, mainly naturally occurring _____.
e: Traces of radioactive materials can be found in the human body, mainly naturally occurring potassium-40. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The radioactive gas, _____, can be found at higher levels in the air in houses and underground water sources.
e: The radioactive gas, argon, can be found at higher levels in the air in houses and underground water sources. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Prolonged exposure to radon gas can cause _____ cancer.
e: Prolonged exposure to radon gas can cause lung cancer. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Uranium-235, americium-241, and plutonium-239 are _____ materials produced from a breeder reactor.
e: Uranium-235, americium-241, and plutonium-239 are fissile materials produced from a breeder reactor. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Ionisation smoke detectors use _____ as a source of alpha particles.
e: Ionisation smoke detectors use americium-241 as a source of alpha particles. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: A well-known use of carbon-14 is radiocarbon dating which can be used to date wooden and _____ objects.
e: A well-known use of carbon-14 is radiocarbon dating which can be used to date wooden and organic objects. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Uranium-235 is used as fuel for nuclear power plants and naval nuclear _____ systems.
e: Uranium-235 is used as fuel for nuclear power plants and naval nuclear propulsion systems. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Caesium-137 is used as a tracer in medical radiation therapy devices for treating _____.
e: Caesium-137 is used as a tracer in medical radiation therapy devices for treating cancer. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Nuclear reactors generate electricity by using fissile heavy atoms instead of _____ fuels.
e: Nuclear reactors generate electricity by using fissile heavy atoms instead of fossil fuels. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The explosion of a nuclear weapon releases a combination of heat, blast waves and _____.
e: The explosion of a nuclear weapon releases a combination of heat, blast waves and radiation. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Radionuclides found in water include potassium-40, radium-226 and _____.
e: Radionuclides found in water include potassium-40, radium-226 and oxygen-16. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Radioactive materials can enter the human body through water and food and may be accumulated in blood and certain vital _____.
e: Radioactive materials can enter the human body through water and food and may be accumulated in blood and certain vital organs. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Radioactive pollution is the result of released _____ in the environment.
e: Radioactive pollution is the result of released radionuclides in the environment. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: A radionuclide is an atom with an unstable nucleus which has excessive _____.
e: A radionuclide is an atom with an unstable nucleus which has excessive energy. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.
